newsitem.title: CANADA: Hollinger says won't increase Southam bid.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger says won't increase Southam bid.

text.p: Hollinger Inc reaffirmed on Tuesday that it would not increase its bid for the minority shares of Southam Inc, despite recent comments by some minority shareholders that the offer was undervalued.
"We've been pretty consistent since the day we went out there -- no, we're not increasing the bid," said Jack Boultbee, vice-president of finance and treasury at Hollinger.

Hollinger bid C$23.50 a share for the 49 percent of the Southam newspaper chain it did not already own. But analysts said earlier today they expected Hollinger Chief Executive Conrad Black to sweeten the C$923 million offer.
Southam shares were up 0.25 at 22.75 in afternoon trading today on the Toronto Stock Exchange in anticipation of a sweetened bid.

Some minority shareholders have said the bid should be at least C$25 a share. The offer included C$13.50 a share in cash and a C$10 non-voting special share in Hollinger Canadian, a unit of Hollinger International Inc.

Black told reporters at Hollinger's annual meeting on May 27 that he would consider increasing the cash portion of the offer but not the bid's overall value. Boultbee said the comments were blown out of proportion.

"You're reading too much into a very narrow statement. Mr Black said at the meeting that if we were very close, like only a few shares short, he would consider a very minor adjustment to the cash price. But we have no idea what shares have been tendered yet, so we couldn't obviously know right now whether we're very close," Boultbee said in a telephone interview.
He said the bid was a fair value.
"We've stated it. We have our external valuation -- it's not undervalued," Boultbee said.
Southam's independent directors were expected to make a recommendation to shareholders on the bid sometime this week.
Black's offer would fail if it was rejected by at least 33.33 percent of minority shareholders.
